title: Small results: verb complements
summary: Glue a one-syllable outcome onto a verb to say whether the action finished, worked, or landed.
attribution: Original content authored for this project.

blocks.body: Chinese often adds a short second verb right after the first to report the result. That unit is called a resultative complement. 听完 tīng wán (listen till it is done), 写完 xiě wán (write it all out), 看懂 kàn dǒng (read till you understand), 找到 zhǎo dào (search and land on it), 听见 tīng jiàn (hear it), 看见 kàn jiàn (see it), 记住 jì zhù (keep it in mind), 说错 shuō cuò (say it wrongly), 学会 xué huì (learn it through). Because it is one unit, 了 le goes after the whole complement: 我找到了 wǒ zhǎodào le, 他看见了 tā kànjiàn le. Saying 我买了一本书 wǒ mǎi le yì běn shū with no complement is fine but blunter: it reports the act, not the success.

Some complements have grown so tight they carry a special flavour: 到 dào for reaching a target (看到 kàn dào, 买到 mǎi dào), 见 jiàn for perception (看见 kàn jiàn, 听见 tīng jiàn), 懂 dǒng for comprehension (听懂 tīng dǒng, 看懂 kàn dǒng), 完 wán for finishing (吃完饭 chī wán fàn), 好 hǎo for a satisfactory completion (饭做好了 fàn zuò hǎo le, 作业写好了 zuòyè xiě hǎo le), 错 cuò for a slip (拿错鞋 ná cuò xié, 听错名字 tīng cuò míngzi), and 住 zhù for holding fast (记住 jì zhù). To deny a result, 没 méi goes before the verb and 了 le is not added: 我没找到 wǒ méi zhǎodào, 他没听懂 tā méi tīng dǒng.

body.speaker: A
body.py: nǐ tīng dǒng nàgè yǔfǎ le ma?
body.en: Did you understand that grammar point?

body.speaker: B
body.zh: 第一遍没听懂，后来听懂了。
body.py: dì yī biàn méi tīng dǒng, hòulái tīng dǒng le.
body.en: I missed it the first time, then I got it.

body.speaker: B
body.zh: 还没写完。你帮我看看好吗？
body.py: hái méi xiě wán. nǐ bāng wǒ kànkan hǎo ma?
body.en: Not yet. Could you take a look for me?

blocks.title: Practise these
body: 请把这句话读三遍。 qǐng bǎ zhè jù huà dú sān biàn. — Please read this sentence three times.
我没找到我的钥匙。 wǒ méi zhǎodào wǒ de yàoshi. — I did not find my keys.
你在哪里学会的中文？ nǐ zài nǎlǐ xué huì de Zhōngwén? — Where did you learn Chinese?
我听了半天，没听懂。 wǒ tīng le bàntiān, méi tīng dǒng. — I listened for ages and did not understand.
他记错了那个房间号。 tā jì cuò le nàgè fángjiān hào. — He got that room number wrong.
先把名字写好，再交给我。 xiān bǎ míngzi xiě hǎo, zài jiāo gěi wǒ. — Write your name first, then hand it to me.

blocks.body: Independent, unofficial practice material written from scratch for general learners of Mandarin. It teaches verb-resultative complements, and nothing in it is taken from, copied from, or aligned to any commercial course, textbook brand, app, or official exam. It is not an answer key for any test.
